title: Audit Findings Should Be Derived Records
seoTitle: Reproducible Audit Findings: Evidence, Rules and Review
subtitle: Keep the evidence and reasoning behind each audit claim recoverable.
seoDescription: Trace audit findings from saved captures through observations, versioned rules and review. Preserve gaps and verify resolution across the agreed scope.

artwork.alt: Captured evidence passes through transparent rule plates into a sealed monochrome finding record.
artwork.label: Audit lineage / sealed findings
artwork.caption: Artifacts pass through versioned rules before becoming traceable, reviewable finding records.

author: SULAYMAN BOWLES
thesis: A defensible finding names the observations and rule that produced it. Preserve their versions, gaps, and review decisions so an amended claim can be explained rather than merely overwritten.

conclusion.title: Require evidence of the changed condition
conclusion.content: A merged repair is implementation evidence. Resolution needs a new evaluation across the agreed scope, connected to the accepted finding and disclosing new gaps. Keep the earlier evidence and interpretation available for comparison.

evidenceBoundary: Provenance makes derivation inspectable; it does not make the observation complete or the rule correct. Findings still require scope, data-quality checks, domain review, and explicit treatment of measurement gaps.
content: “Missing canonicals” is the end of a pipeline, not an observation. The audit first captured a response, extracted fields, normalized them, applied a rule, grouped URLs, assessed impact, and proposed a change. Collapsing those steps into a label makes the conclusion difficult to reproduce or revise.

Keep artifacts immutable and observations tied to their fields. Versioned rules produce evaluations; findings group them into scoped claims with confidence and gaps. Append review decisions, then keep recommendations as proposals rather than facts inside the observation.

sections.title: Separate capture, interpretation, and action
paragraphs: An artifact is a response, DOM, screenshot, log slice, sitemap, configuration, or analytics export. An observation extracts a typed fact: status 200, no source canonical, or three crawlable inlinks. Retain its artifact pointer, extractor version, capture time, and completeness.

Evaluations record rule identity and version, inputs, parameters, and outcome. A finding can then claim that a template emits conflicting source and DOM canonicals on 184 reviewed URLs. Reviews preserve decisions without overwriting it; recommendations name a change, owner, risk, and acceptance test.

Each layer can fail differently. Authentic captures may be incomplete; correct extraction may describe an unrepresentative scenario; deterministic rules may encode the wrong requirement; sound findings may lead to impractical recommendations. Separation lets reviewers locate their disagreement.

sections.title: Identify inputs, activities, and revisions
paragraphs: W3C PROV distinguishes entities, activities, and agents; OpenLineage tracks runs, jobs, inputs, outputs, and event state. An audit need not adopt either whole vocabulary. It needs input identities, the generating activity, responsible software or reviewer, and time.

Identify bounded runs, artifacts by hash and storage identity, and observations by location and extractor version. Separate rule IDs from their versions. Let a finding retain its issue ID while each claim revision receives a distinct version, making amendment visible.

Propagate correlation through fetch, render, extract, evaluate, review, and export. Trace Context can connect distributed requests, but sampled, short-lived, or asynchronous traces still need durable domain IDs. Correlation locates events; provenance records derivation.
bullets: Do not use mutable filenames as the only artifact identity.
Separate rule identity from code deployment identity.
Retain the exact input set for every evaluation.
Make review actor and automation identity explicit.
Carry run and URL identity into every export row.
Record sampling and missing-event states when telemetry is incomplete.

sections.title: Test prerequisites before the finding
paragraphs: Rules need required fields, eligibility, parameters, outcomes, and gap behavior. A failed parser, non-HTML response, incomplete render, or intentionally documentless route cannot automatically become “missing title.” Check prerequisites and return not-applicable or insufficient-evidence when they fail.

Version logic, thresholds, normalization, and required-input changes. Keep a readable summary and executable reference. New rules applied to old artifacts create new evaluations, leaving historical issue counts explainable.

Record evaluation time for clock-dependent checks and captures or dataset versions for external lookups. Learned classification needs model, prompt or feature versions, confidence, and review thresholds. Materially variable results require an explicit trial or sampling contract.

codeExamples.title: A normalized schema for lineage-preserving evaluations
codeExamples.description: The composite key prevents a new rule run from overwriting an earlier interpretation.
codeExamples.code:
CREATE TABLE rule_evaluation (
  run_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  url_key TEXT NOT NULL,
  rule_id TEXT NOT NULL,
  rule_version TEXT NOT NULL,
  input_set_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
  outcome TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (outcome IN
    ("pass", "fail", "gap", "not_applicable")),
  evidence_json TEXT NOT NULL,
  evaluated_at TEXT NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (run_id, url_key, rule_id, rule_version, input_set_hash)
);

sections.title: Keep gaps in the denominator
paragraphs: Blocked fetches, timed-out renders, unsupported formats, authentication, and incomplete inventories are observations about coverage. Give them codes and evidence. Do not turn every gap into failure or quietly remove it from the denominator.
Name the uncertainty behind confidence: parser certainty, classification strength, affected-set coverage, or implementation assumptions. One unlabeled percentage cannot answer all four questions.

“184 of 210 eligible product URLs failed; 17 additional URLs had incomplete renders” states the counted population and separate gap. “87.6% issue confidence” hides what was measured. Preserve counts, eligibility, and denominators so the reviewer can inspect both.

sections.title: Preserve review history through export
paragraphs: Append acceptance, rejection, evidence requests, duplicate decisions, risk changes, scope amendments, and revised recommendations to a finding version. Show reviewers the claim, affected set, examples, gaps, rule, and artifact links. A final label alone conceals the pipeline under review.

Keep stable IDs in exports. CSV can carry finding and rule versions, URL, outcome, confidence class, gap, evidence reference, review state, owner, and acceptance test; JSON can retain nested lineage. Link readable executive summaries to those underlying records.

After repair, create a fresh run and evaluations linked to the accepted finding. Require implementation evidence and the affected rule passing over the agreed scope, with new gaps disclosed. Ticket closure or merged code does not establish that the condition changed.
bullets: Never overwrite the evidence set after a finding enters review.
Store reviewer amendments as new claim versions.
Keep URL-level rows behind every aggregate.
Export gap states and denominators with pass/fail counts.
Link the implementation change and the validating rerun separately.
Mark a finding resolved only against its acceptance contract.
